St. Mardarije of Libertyville

Saints

St. Mardarije of Libertyville

St. Mardarije Uskoković · St. Mardary of Libertyville

Period
1889–1935
Region
North America
Titles / vocation
Hierarch · Missionary
Commemoration
November 29/December 12 (paired calendars in the 2015 official report)

Introduction

St. Mardarije Uskoković is the Serbian bishop whose missionary and organizational work centered on the American-Canadian diocese and Libertyville.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death from tuberculosis, December 12, 1935, in the official report.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The official report describes birth in Montenegro in 1889, monastic life at Studenitsa from 1907, and theological education in Russia.

[1] Official canonization report and biography · Published biographical account,paragraph 5

Life and notable events

He works in America before episcopal consecration in Belgrade in 1926 and purchases land for Saint Sava Monastery with his own funds.

[1] Official canonization report and biography · Published biographical account,paragraph 6

The 2015 account follows the disruption after the Russian Revolution: after participation in the 1919 All-American Sobor, he returns to Belgrade and serves at Rakovitsa. It describes assistance to Bishop Nikolai in organizing the American diocese, and later the 1927 national assembly and 1931 clergy conference. These institutional episodes show the work behind the title of first ruling Serbian bishop in North America.

[1] Official canonization report and biography · Published biographical account,paragraph 3; Published biographical account,paragraph 5; Published biographical account,paragraph 7

Death and martyrdom

The report states that he continued working while gravely ill with tuberculosis and died on December 12, 1935, aged46.

[1] Official canonization report and biography · Published biographical account,paragraph 7

Writings and legacy

The 2015 announcement gives a paired-calendar commemoration. The distinct 2017 report below records the later glorification services and relics.

[1] Official canonization report and biography · Published biographical account,paragraph 3; Published biographical account,paragraph 4; Published biographical account,paragraph 5 · [2] Official glorification report · Published biographical account,paragraph 9; Published biographical account,paragraph 15

The July 2017 report describes the three-day gathering in Illinois, with Patriarch Irinej presiding and Orthodox hierarchs from several jurisdictions attending. It places the services at New Gracanica and Saint Sava monasteries. It reports the May 2017 uncovering of Mardarije’s relics and describes their liturgical welcome and veneration during the glorification weekend. Metropolitan Tikhon and Bishop Paul participated from the OCA. These are the report’s distinct 2017 events; the repeated earlier life narrative on the same page is not counted as a separate source for additional biography.

[2] Official glorification report · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3; Published biographical account,paragraph 6; Published biographical account,paragraph 8; Published biographical account,paragraph 9

The elders which are among you I exhort, who am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed:

Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind;

Neither as being lords over God’s heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.

And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.

Related Scripture; not a claim that this passage narrates the saint’s life or is a prescribed feast-day reading.

[3] Public-domain Bible translation · 1 Peter 5: 1–4

The event report also records a symposium on his life, a documentary presentation, and participation by clergy and choirs from several Orthodox communities, including ROCOR. The Sunday homily drew on his 1935 Paschal encyclical. A procession followed the glorification Liturgy, and the report identifies the monastery as the shrine of his relics. These are specific features of the 2017 commemoration, not instructions for visitors to reproduce the service.

[2] Official glorification report · Published biographical account,paragraph 4; Published biographical account,paragraph 5; Published biographical account,paragraph 8; Published biographical account,paragraph 9
